blocks.text: *Lesson Twenty-Eight* — the opening page of this lesson (printed page 156) is missing from the original scan.

items.q: Is Vicky looking at herself in the mirror?
Is Louis combing his hair himself?
Is Claudia doing her homework by herself?
Do the girls brush their teeth by themselves?
Does Mr. Garcia hit himself with the table?
Does the dog wash itself in the tub?
Are the boys painting the walls by themselves?
Can we finish this work by ourselves?
Can the child cut his finger by himself?

blocks.text:
*Can you wash yourself “if” you don’t have any water?*
*No, I can’t wash myself “if” I don’t have any water.*

items.q: Can you brush your teeth yourself if you don’t have a toothbrush?
Can Louis comb himself if he doesn’t have a comb?
Can Vicky look at herself in the mirror if she doesn’t have one?
Can Timmy wash itself if there isn’t any water in the tub?

blocks.text: *TOO HEAVY* is the opposite of *VERY LIGHT*

items.q: Can you speak English perfectly? (too complex)
Can you buy a Rolls Royce? (too expensive)
Can you drive an airplane? (too difficult)
Can you turn the air conditioner off? (too hot)
Can I climb up a mountain without equipment? (too risky)
Why can’t you take care of my baby? (too little)
Why can’t you eat a hamburger or a pizza? (too fat)
Why can’t she help you with the housework? (too lazy)
Why can’t she come with you? (too busy)
Why don’t you drive to Chile? (too far)

blocks.text:
*ENOUGH MEANS SUFFICIENT.*
*ENOUGH PRECEDES NOUNS AND FOLLOWS ADJECTIVES.*   _Enough_ + Noun · _Adjective_ + Enough

items.q: Can you reach the light? (_tall_)
Can she eat a big dinner now? (hungry)
Can he drink five glasses of water now? (thirsty)
Can we study together? (books)
Can they get into the car? (space)
Can you buy an airplane? (rich)
Can we sit here? (chairs)
Can you run 100 miles? (strong)
Can he talk to an American now? (_fluent_)
Can she be in a beauty contest? (pretty)
